question: How do I get from Deggendorf train station to the campus?
expected_behavior: About a 20-minute walk, or city buses 1, 2 and 3, which run every 20 minutes between the station and the campus.
answer: You can walk from Deggendorf train station to the DIT campus in about 20 minutes, or take bus 1, 2 or 3; buses run every 20 minutes. [1] Check live timetables with the transport provider, as journey times and schedules may vary. [1]

question: is there a semester ticket for DIT students?
expected_behavior: No semester-ticket agreement for TH Deggendorf at the moment; students can still buy the discounted student ticket (Bavarian discount ticket) via the VAG subscription portal.
answer: No. TH Deggendorf currently has no semester-ticket agreement, so its students cannot buy a semester-ticket surcharge ticket. [2][3] Students can still purchase the separate discounted student ticket through VAG; check the VAG subscription portal for current details. [2]

question: My room in a student residence has its own door on a shared hallway. Do I have to pay the broadcasting fee for it?
expected_behavior: Yes: a room on a generally accessible hallway counts as a dwelling, so the fee (18.36 euros per month) is due per room, even with its own bathroom or kitchen. If several rooms share one front door, the flat-share rules apply.
answer: Yes. A room opening onto a generally accessible shared hallway is treated as its own dwelling, so the fee is €18.36 per month for that room; your own bathroom or kitchen does not change this. [1] Student status alone does not exempt you. [1]

question: What should I do if I get sick at night or on the weekend?
expected_behavior: Emergency: call 112 or go to a hospital. Urgent but not an emergency: call the on-call doctors at 116 117 or find a 'Bereitschaftspraxis' in the city.
answer: If it’s an emergency, go to a hospital or call **112** for immediate treatment. [1] If it’s urgent but not an emergency and you can’t wait for your GP, call **116 117** to reach an on-call doctor, or look for a **“Bereitschaftspraxis”** (on-call clinic) in Deggendorf. [1] When arranging care, mention your type of health insurance so you can find the right doctor. [1]

question: Do I need a referral from my GP to see a dentist?
expected_behavior: No referral is needed for some areas, for example dentist, gynaecologist or orthopaedist; normally the GP is the first stop and gives referrals to other specialists.
answer: No. You do not need a GP referral to see a dentist in Germany. [1] When booking, mention your health-insurance type so the practice can confirm it is suitable for you. [1]

question: I have statutory health insurance from an EU country. Is it still enough if I start a part-time job here?
expected_behavior: No: with a paid internship or a part-time job while studying, coverage with a German provider is required; home-country insurance is not sufficient then.
answer: No. Although EU students with statutory insurance may usually have it recognised in Germany, the guidance says that if you have a part-time job while studying, your home-country insurance is not considered sufficient and you must obtain coverage with a German provider [1]. Contact a German statutory health insurance provider about your coverage; for DIT, insurance confirmation must be sent electronically before enrolment [2].

question: How much money do I need in a blocked account for a German student visa?
expected_behavior: At least 11,904 euros (2026); funds can also be proven with a scholarship or a declaration of commitment.
answer: For a German **study visa**, you need at least **€11,904 in a blocked account in 2026**; this covers the financial proof requirement for your study programme [1][3]. Other accepted proof includes a scholarship or a declaration of commitment [1].

question: For how long is a residence permit for studying usually issued?
expected_behavior: Usually for an initial two years; if the degree is not finished, it can be renewed for another two years.
answer: In Germany, a residence permit for study purposes is usually issued for an initial period of two years. If you have not completed your degree by then, you can request a further two-year renewal. [1]

question: After I graduate, can I stay in Germany to look for a job?
expected_behavior: Yes: a residence permit for jobseekers (Section 20 (1) No. 1 AufenthG) for up to 18 months; any work is allowed while looking for skilled employment.
answer: Yes. After successfully completing your degree, you can apply for a jobseeker residence permit for up to 18 months to find skilled employment, and you may work in any occupation while looking [1]. Once you find qualified employment, you can apply to change to a skilled-worker residence permit or an EU Blue Card [1].

question: how do i connect to the wifi on campus
expected_behavior: Use the WLAN 'eduroam' (setup page th-deg.de/en/eduroam) or '@BayernWlan'; for off-campus access there is the eduVPN.
answer: DIT lists **eduroam** and **@BayernWlan** as campus Wi‑Fi networks; for setup instructions, use the [eduroam guide](https://th-de.de/en/eduroam). [2] If you have trouble connecting, contact the IT service desk at **it-support@th-de.de**. [2]

question: How can I print documents at the university?
expected_behavior: Register the student card at a printer with a card reader, then load credit at the terminal next to the copy shop (room C012); copy-shop staff in building C, room C012 help with printer problems.
answer: Register your student card at a printer with a card reader, then add credit at the terminal next to the copyshop in Building C, Room C012. [1] For printer problems such as paper jams or missing paper, contact the copyshop staff in Building C, Room C012, at +49 991 3615-362. [1]

question: What will my DIT email address look like?
expected_behavior: name.surname@stud.th-deg.de; if the name already exists, a number is added (name.surname2@...). The address can be checked at idm.th-deg.de (on campus or via VPN).
answer: Your DIT student email will usually look like **name.surname@stud.th-deg.de**. If that address is already in use, consecutive numbers are added, for example **name.surname2@stud.th-deg.de**. You can check your exact address at **idm.th-deg.de** while on campus or connected via VPN. [4]

question: How much is the rent at the Bahnhofstrasse student residence?
expected_behavior: 306.05 to 454 euros for a single apartment, depending on size; about 360 euros (359.54 to 360.14) per person in a two-person shared flat.
answer: At the Bahnhofstrasse student residence, a complete single apartment costs €306.05–€454 per month, depending on size; a room in a shared flat for two costs €359.54–€360.14 per month. [1]

question: Who at DIT helps international students with entry and residence formalities?
expected_behavior: The Welcome Centre, the first point of contact for international students; email welcome@th-deg.de.
answer: DIT’s Welcome Centre is the first point of contact for international students and prospective students, and provides guidance with entry and residence formalities. Contact **welcome@th-deg.de**. [1]

question: I want to email a staff member about enrolling in a course. What should my email include?
expected_behavior: Send from the student email account to the right contact person, with a clear subject, formal salutation, matriculation number, course of study/semester and course number, a precise request, and a formal close with the full name. Do not send it to several people or mark it urgent.
answer: Use your student email account and send one message to the right contact person. [3] Include a meaningful subject, a formal salutation, your first and last name, matriculation number, course of study and semester, and a precise request naming the course you want to enrol in. [1][3] Write in full sentences with correct spelling and punctuation, use polite language, and close formally (for example, “Kind regards”) with your full name. [1][3] The DIT example subject is “Enrolment in German course A1 / 1+2 Nr. 88122”; reply to an existing email thread rather than starting a new one. [1]

question: What documents do I need to open a bank account, and where do I get the registration certificate?
expected_behavior: Usually passport, residence permit, registration certificate and possibly a payslip (D22). The registration is done at the Buergeramt Deggendorf within two weeks of moving in, with ID/passport and the landlord's move-in confirmation (D30).
answer: Banks generally ask for a valid passport, residence permit and registration certificate; a payslip may also be required depending on the account type, and requirements vary by bank. [1] The passages do not say where to obtain the registration certificate, so check with your local registration authority. The “admission registration certificate” mentioned by DIT is a different document and is used to find your matriculation number. [4]

question: Where is the foreigners office in Deggendorf, and who at DIT can help me before I go there?
expected_behavior: Foreign Nationals Office at the Administrative District Office, Herrenstrasse 18, phone 0991 3100-420 (D26); DIT's Welcome Centre (welcome@th-deg.de) helps with entry and residence formalities (D10).
answer: The Foreign Nationals Office (responsible for right of residence) is at Herrenstraße 18 in Deggendorf [2]. Before going, contact DIT’s Welcome Centre, the first point of contact for international students with residence-formality questions, at welcome@th-deg.de [4]. The office is by appointment only; the appointment guidance is an English translation, and the original official page is authoritative [3].

question: Which is cheaper for a single apartment: Bahnhofstrasse or Finkenhof Frauenstrasse?
expected_behavior: Bahnhofstrasse 306.05 to 454 euros; Frauenstrasse 315 to 354 euros for a single apartment. The cheapest starts at Bahnhofstrasse, but the ranges overlap and depend on size; Frauenstrasse has the lower maximum.
answer: The listed rent ranges are €306.05–€454 for a Bahnhofstrasse single apartment [5] and €315–€354 for a Finkenhof Frauenstrasse single apartment [2]. Bahnhofstrasse has the lower starting price, but Finkenhof has the lower maximum, so which is cheaper depends on the specific apartment; the passages don’t state the period these rents apply to.

question: Can my student job help me prove enough money to renew my residence permit? How much do I need?
expected_behavior: Generally yes: as a student assistant you can act as your own guarantor if you have at least 992 euros per month (2026) from the job; check with the foreigners authority first (D23). Initial visa funding is different (blocked account, D21).
answer: If you work as a student assistant in a company in Germany, your job can generally help you prove funding for a residence-permit renewal; in 2026, you must show at least €992 per month available from that secondary income, and the job need not be indefinite [1]. Whether this applies to other types of student jobs is not specified; check with your competent foreigners authority [1]. What kind of student job do you have?

question: I'm looking for a room in a WG in Deggendorf. Where can I search, and who pays the TV licence in a WG?
expected_behavior: DIT Wohnungsboerse (no account needed to search), flat websites and social media, start about 3 months ahead, help via accommodation-dit@th-deg.de (D08). In a WG only one resident pays the licence fee; exemption only if everyone qualifies (D25).
answer: Search early—WG vacancies may be posted up to three months before move-in—and try wg-gesucht.de, the Studierendenwerk room exchange, DIT’s accommodation listings, campus noticeboard by the canteen and café in the F-Building, plus rental websites and social media using “WG” or “WG-Zimmer” with “Deggendorf.” [1][3][4] In a WG, one resident registers and pays the TV licence for the dwelling; other residents who have registered can deregister, and if asked to clarify your obligation, give the contribution number of the person paying. [2] An exemption is possible only if every occupant meets its requirements. [2]
